The IRGC’s National Aerospace Park missile museum is going to need a brand-new wing to accommodate all the enemy weaponry Iran has been capturing. Besides the freshly procured REMUS 600 drone spy sub, Iran has collected:
🔴 [an Anduril Dive-LD drone sub](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74351)
🔴 a largely intact MQ-9 Reaper
🔴[ Israeli Hermes 450 and 900 series UAVs](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73415)
🔴 remains of a US F-15E Strike Eagle, two Black Hawk helicopters and a C-130 transport aircraft
🔴 a GAU-5A rifle used exclusively by the US Air Force
🔴 an unexploded GBU-39 Small Diameter Bomb, GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrator bunker buster and stealth JASSM missile
🔴 an unexploded Tomahawk warhead
 
That’s adding to the array of systems Iran captured before the current war, including:
 
♦️ an RQ-170 Sentinel, hijacked by Iran will conducting illegal reconnaissance in 2011
♦️ a $220M RQ-4A Global Hawk, downed over Hormuz in 2019 and put on display
♦️ A Boeing ScanEagle
♦️ AeroVironment RQ-11 Raven and AAI RQ-7 Shadow drones
 
With the latest haul, weapons experts can expect a reverse-engineered Iranian REMUS 600, but 10-30 times cheaper, in the near future. Or even a totally new indigenous design borrowing a handful of the US tech’s components.

🗣IRGC adds US REMUS 600 spy drone sub to its collection
 
The autonomous underwater vehicle was found operating in Hormuz Strait. The IRGC says its capture was made possible thanks to a coordinated intel and EW operation.
The sub is the second waterborne drone vehicle Iran has captured in less than a month. On September 8, the IRGC Navy seized an Anduril Dive-LD recon, seabed mapping and [inspection submersible.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74258)
Iran’s Houthi allies captured a REMUS 600 in 2018, and used it to help build a technically less sophisticated but strategically superior [autonomous torpedo.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74821)
